definition_en: a group of people who live in the same area or share the same interest, religion or way of life
core_image: 一条街上的人共用同一口水井，彼此点头问好
scene: 小区里，邻居们一起清理被风吹倒的树枝。The whole community came out to clear the fallen branches.
sceneCN: 这里 community 指「社区」（第 1 个义项：住在同一片地方的人）；句意是整个社区的人都出来清理倒下的树枝。

senses.title: People of one area
senses.definition: the people who live in one particular area and often share services
senses.definitionCN: 住在某一地区、常常共用设施的一群人
senses.example: The whole community uses the new sports ground.
senses.exampleCN: 整个社区都在使用这块新运动场。
senses.why: People who live close by share roads, shops and schools, so they form a natural unit.
senses.whyCN: 住得近的人共用道路、商店和学校，自然就形成了一个单位。

senses.title: A group with one interest
senses.definition: a group of people who share an interest, a religion or a job
senses.definitionCN: 因共同的兴趣、信仰或职业而聚在一起的一群人
senses.example: She joined the online community for young writers.
senses.exampleCN: 她加入了年轻写作者的线上社群。
senses.why: Shared interest, not shared space, holds this group together.
senses.whyCN: 把这群人连在一起的是共同兴趣，而不是同一片地方。

senses.title: A feeling of belonging
senses.definition: the feeling that you belong to a group and care about its members
senses.definitionCN: 觉得自己属于某个群体并关心其成员的感觉
senses.example: The small school has a real sense of community.
senses.exampleCN: 这所小学校有一种真切的归属感。
senses.why: From shared life comes a shared identity, which people also call community.
senses.whyCN: 共同生活生出共同的身份感，人们也把这叫作 community。

intro.en: Community comes from Latin communis, meaning shared or common, and first named a body of people who held things in common.
intro.cn: community 来自拉丁语 communis，意为共有的、公共的，最初指共同拥有某些东西的一群人。

items.en: Communis meant shared by many, not owned by one.
items.cn: communis 意为由许多人共有，而非一人独享。

items.en: Communitas named the state of sharing and the group that shared.
items.cn: communitas 指共有状态，也指共有东西的那群人。

items.en: Old French communete carried the word into everyday use.
items.cn: 古法语 communete 把这个词带进日常使用。

items.en: English community first meant a body of people with common rights.
items.cn: 英语 community 最初指享有共同权利的一群人。

items.en: It now covers neighbourhoods, online groups and the international community.
items.cn: 如今它覆盖邻里、线上群体以及国际社会。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that echo the shape of community, and the meaning group names other ways of speaking about people who belong together.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 community 形似的词，近义组列出其他指一群人彼此归属的说法。

entries.definition: a group of people who live together and share everything
entries.definitionCN: 共同生活、共享一切的公社

entries.definition: a political system in which property belongs to the state

people living together in an organised way
the area around the place where you live
a number of people or things gathered together

normalIntro.en: These hooks start from a shared well, then move to shared interests and to the feeling of belonging.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从共用一口井开始，再走到共同兴趣与归属感。

normal.en: Com- means together, so a community is people held together by something.
normal.cn: com- 表示一起，所以 community 就是被某种东西连在一起的人。

normal.en: Same street gives one kind of community; same hobby gives another.
normal.cn: 同一条街是一种社区，同一个爱好是另一种社区。

normal.en: You can belong to a community without living in it.
normal.cn: 你不必住在其中，也能属于一个社群。

normal.en: Commune and community share the same old root of sharing.
normal.cn: commune 与 community 共享同一个表示共有的古老词根。

normal.en: A sense of community is the warm feeling, not the map.
normal.cn: 归属感是那种温暖的感觉，而不是地图上的界线。

abstract.en: Picture neighbours passing bread over the same low wall.
abstract.cn: 想象邻居隔着同一道矮墙递面包。

abstract.en: Picture a forum where strangers answer a question at midnight.
abstract.cn: 想象一个论坛，陌生人在午夜回答问题。

abstract.en: Picture a whole street sweeping leaves after a storm.
abstract.cn: 想象整条街的人在暴风雨后一起扫落叶。

examples.en: The whole community helped rebuild the damaged school.
examples.cn: 整个社区都来帮忙重建受损的学校。

examples.en: He is well known in the local business community.
examples.cn: 他在当地商业圈里很有名。

examples.en: Online communities let shy people find friends.
examples.cn: 线上社群让害羞的人找到朋友。

root: 源自拉丁语 communis（共有的），经 communitas 进入法语与英语，本义是共同拥有某些东西的一群人，后指社区、群体与共同体感。

sensesIntro.en: From people sharing one place, to people sharing one interest, and finally to the warm feeling of belonging.
sensesIntro.cn: 从共居一地的人，到共享一种兴趣的人，最后到那份温暖的归属感。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: neighbours around one well, greeting each other by name.
core.cn: 核心意象：一条街上的人共用同一口水井，彼此点头问好。

branches.en: Sharing a place is the oldest sense of community.
branches.cn: 共用一片地方是 community 最古老的义项。

branches.en: Sharing an interest creates a community without walls.
branches.cn: 共享一种兴趣，就能造出没有围墙的社群。

branches.en: The feeling of belonging is the inward side of community.
branches.cn: 归属感是 community 向内的一面。

branches.en: Both rest on something held in common.
branches.cn: 两者都建立在某种共有的东西之上。

branches.en: A group you care about also cares back.
branches.cn: 你在意的群体，也会反过来在意你。

intro.en: Community is built on the Latin base commun- plus the noun ending -ity.
intro.cn: community 由拉丁词基 commun- 加名词后缀 -ity 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin communis supplied the idea of something held in common.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 communis 提供了「共有」这一核心意思。

items.example: The building has a communal kitchen.

items.meaning: a group that lives and shares together
items.example: They joined a small commune in the hills.
items.exampleCN: 他们加入了山里一个小公社。

items.example: The meal became a kind of communion.
items.exampleCN: 那顿饭成了某种共享的时刻。

items.meaning: a person who shares ideas well

items.example: The two towns share a common market.

definition_en: a person who spends time with you or travels with you, or a thing that goes with another
core_image: 旅途中并肩走着的两个人，一左一右踩着同一段影子
scene: 雨夜里，老人把伞往同伴那边偏了偏。He walked slowly so his companion could keep up.
sceneCN: 这里 companion 指「同伴」（第 1 个义项：与你同行的人）；句意是他放慢脚步，好让同伴跟上。

senses.title: A person who goes with you
senses.definition: a person who spends time with you or goes somewhere with you
senses.definitionCN: 与你共度时光或一同前往某处的人
senses.example: Her dog was her only companion on long walks.
senses.exampleCN: 长距离散步时，她的狗是唯一的同伴。
senses.why: A companion is defined by shared time, not by a shared address.
senses.whyCN: 同伴由共度的时光来定义，而不是由同一个住址来定义。

senses.title: A thing that matches another
senses.definition: one of a pair of things that are designed to go together
senses.definitionCN: 设计上成对、配套使用的事物之一
senses.example: This book is a companion to the earlier dictionary.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书是早前那部词典的配套卷。
senses.why: Objects, like people, can be paired so that each answers the other.
senses.whyCN: 物件和人都能配对，彼此呼应。

senses.title: A handbook for a place
senses.definition: a book that gives information for visitors or users
senses.definitionCN: 为访客或使用者提供信息的书
senses.example: He bought a companion to the old city.
senses.exampleCN: 他买了一本古城指南。
senses.why: A guide walks beside you in words, so it is called a companion.
senses.whyCN: 指南用文字陪你走，所以也被叫作 companion。

intro.en: Companion comes from Latin com, together, and panis, bread: a companion was the person who shared your bread.
intro.cn: companion 来自拉丁语 com（一起）与 panis（面包）：companion 本指与你分面包的人。

items.en: Com panis described one who ate bread with another.
items.cn: com panis 指与另一个人一同吃面包的人。

items.en: Companio named a fellow soldier who shared the daily ration.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语 companio 指分食每日口粮的战友。

items.en: Old French compaignon widened the word to any comrade.
items.cn: 古法语 compaignon 把这个词扩展到任何伙伴。

items.en: English companion first meant a person who shared a journey.
items.cn: 英语 companion 最初指共走一段路的人。

items.en: It grew to cover matching books and travel guides.
items.cn: 后来它扩展到配套的书与旅行指南。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in shape to companion, and the meaning group names other people or things that stay beside you.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 companion 形状相近的词，近义组列出其他陪伴在侧的人或物。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with shared bread, then move to shared roads and to the books that walk beside us.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从分面包开始，再走到同行的路与陪我们走的手册。

normal.en: Com- is together and pan- is bread, so a companion is a bread mate.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，pan- 是面包，companion 就是分面包的人。

normal.en: A companion shares your time, not necessarily your home.
normal.cn: 同伴分享的是你的时间，不一定是你的住处。

normal.en: A companion volume is a book paired with another book.
normal.cn: 配套卷就是与另一本书成对的书。

normal.en: A travel guide is a companion because it goes with you.
normal.cn: 旅行指南是 companion，因为它跟着你走。

normal.en: Companionship is the warm noun behind the person.
normal.cn: companionship 是这个人背后那个温暖的抽象名词。

abstract.en: Picture two walkers under one umbrella in the rain.
abstract.cn: 想象雨中两个人同撑一把伞。

abstract.en: Picture a dog waiting by the door every evening.
abstract.cn: 想象一只狗每天傍晚在门口等候。

abstract.en: Picture two books standing side by side on a shelf.
abstract.cn: 想象两本书并排立在书架上。

examples.en: Her sister was her closest companion during the trip.
examples.cn: 旅途中她妹妹是她最亲近的同伴。

examples.en: The old man's companion was a small grey cat.
examples.cn: 老人的伴侣是一只小灰猫。

examples.en: This workbook is a companion to the main text.
examples.cn: 这本练习册是主教材的配套用书。

branches.en: A matching object answers the first like a second voice.
branches.cn: 配对之物像第二个声音一样回应第一个。

branches.en: A guidebook is a companion made of paper.
branches.cn: 指南是用纸做的同伴。

branches.en: Person and object both keep someone from being alone.
branches.cn: 人和物都在让人不至于孤单。

branches.en: A companion volume and a guide both complete a set.
branches.cn: 配套卷与指南都让一套东西变得完整。

definition_en: a business that sells goods or services, or the state of being with other people
core_image: 会议桌旁一群人围着同一份文件讨论
scene: 夜深了，主人留客人在客厅再坐一会儿。I enjoy your company, so please stay a little longer.
sceneCN: 这里 company 指「陪伴」（第 2 个义项：有人陪在身边）；句意是我喜欢有你陪着，请再坐一会儿。

senses.title: A business
senses.definition: an organisation that sells goods or services to make money
senses.definitionCN: 以销售商品或服务来盈利的组织
senses.example: She works for a small software company.
senses.exampleCN: 她在一家小型软件公司工作。
senses.why: A group of people acting as one legal person is the modern core of the word.
senses.whyCN: 一群人作为一个法人行动，这是这个词现代的核义。

senses.title: Being with people
senses.definition: the state of being with other people
senses.definitionCN: 与他人待在一起的状态
senses.example: I could use some company this evening.
senses.exampleCN: 今晚我需要有人陪。
senses.why: The old sense of sharing time survives beside the business sense.
senses.whyCN: 共度时光这个古老意思与商业义项并存。

senses.title: A group of performers
senses.definition: a group of actors or dancers who work together
senses.definitionCN: 一起工作的演员或舞者团体
senses.example: The company will perform in three cities.
senses.exampleCN: 剧团将在三座城市演出。
senses.why: Players who travel and work as one body keep the older group meaning alive.
senses.whyCN: 一起巡演、一起工作的演员保留了较早的群体含义。

intro.en: Company shares the Latin bread root: com panis, people who eat bread together.
intro.cn: company 与面包同源：拉丁语 com panis 指一起吃面包的人。

items.en: Com panis meant those who shared a loaf.
items.cn: com panis 指分食一块面包的人。

items.en: Companio was a title for a comrade in arms.
items.cn: companio 是对战友的称呼。

items.en: Old French compaignie named the group itself.
items.cn: 古法语 compaignie 指这群人本身。

items.en: English company first meant a body of people together.
items.cn: 英语 company 最初指聚在一起的一群人。

items.en: Trade guilds turned company into a business word.
items.cn: 行业公会把这个词变成了商业用语。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that resemble company in spelling, and the meaning group names other bodies of people or states of being together.

definition_en: similar enough to be compared with something else, or good enough to be equal to it
core_image: 两把并排放在桌上的尺子，长度几乎一样
scene: 同事把两份方案的报价摊在桌上逐项对照。The two plans are comparable in cost but not in speed.
sceneCN: 这里 comparable 指「可比较的；相当的」（第 1 个义项：能够放在一起比较）；句意是两份方案在成本上相当，在速度上却不同。

pos.zh: 可比较的；类似的；相当的

senses.title: Able to be compared
senses.definition: similar enough in size, value or quality to be compared
senses.definitionCN: 在大小、价值或质量上相似到可以相互比较
senses.example: The two cities are comparable in size.
senses.exampleCN: 这两座城市规模相当。
senses.why: Comparison only works when the two sides stand on common ground.
senses.whyCN: 比较只有在双方有共同基准时才成立。

senses.title: Good enough to match
senses.definition: as good as another thing of the same kind
senses.definitionCN: 与同类事物一样好
senses.example: Her salary is comparable to that of a senior engineer.
senses.exampleCN: 她的薪水相当于一名高级工程师。
senses.why: From being measurable, the word moves to being equal in worth.
senses.whyCN: 从「可以量」进一步引申为「价值相当」。

intro.en: Comparable comes from Latin comparare, to pair things as equals, built on par, equal.
intro.cn: comparable 来自拉丁语 comparare，意为把事物作为同等者放在一起，词基 par 表示相等。

items.en: Par meant equal, level, of the same rank.
items.cn: par 表示相等、齐平、同级。

items.en: Comparare meant to set two things side by side as equals.
items.cn: comparare 意为把两样东西作为同等者并排放置。

items.en: Old French comparer kept the pairing sense.
items.cn: 古法语 comparer 保留了配对比较的意思。

items.en: English comparable first described things of equal measure.
items.cn: 英语 comparable 最初描述分量相等的事物。

items.en: It now covers costs, data and any fair comparison.

root: 源自拉丁语 comparatio，由 comparare（并列比较）加名词后缀而来，本义是把事物并列衡量的动作，后引申为比喻与可比之处。

sensesIntro.en: From the act of comparing, to a stated likeness, and finally to the standard behind a judgement.
sensesIntro.cn: 从比较的动作，到明确说出的类比，最后到判断背后的基准。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two maps spread open, one finger moving between the same two points.
core.cn: 核心意象：桌上摊开两张地图，手指在相同的位置来回移动。

branches.en: The act itself is the plainest sense of the noun.
branches.cn: 动作本身是这个名词最朴素的义项。

branches.en: A likeness spoken aloud is a comparison made of words.
branches.cn: 说出口的相似，就是用语言做成的比较。

branches.en: Every judgement needs a standard to compare against.
branches.cn: 每个判断都需要一个可对照的标准。

branches.en: Both put two things in one frame for the mind to hold.
branches.cn: 两者都把两物放进同一画框，好让心里握住。

branches.en: The act and its standard are two halves of one judgement.
branches.cn: 比较的动作与它的标准，是同一个判断的两半。

intro.en: Comparison is built on the verb compare with the noun ending -ison.
intro.cn: comparison 由动词 compare 加名词后缀 -ison 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin comparatio already joined the act of weighing with its result.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 comparatio 早已把衡量的动作与结果合在一起。

definition_en: an instrument that shows direction, a tool for drawing circles, or the range of something
core_image: 掌心大小的圆盘上，一根磁针轻轻摆动后定住指向北方
scene: 山里起雾，队长掏出小圆盘看指针方向。Without a compass they would have walked in circles.
sceneCN: 这里 compass 指「指南针」（第 1 个义项：指示方向的仪器）；句意是没有指南针，他们就会原地绕圈。

senses.title: The direction finder
senses.definition: an instrument with a magnetic needle that always points north
senses.definitionCN: 带磁针、始终指向北方的仪器
senses.example: The compass swung and settled on north.
senses.exampleCN: 罗盘转了转，停在了北面。
senses.why: A needle that finds north gives the traveller the one fixed line everything else is measured from.
senses.whyCN: 找到北方的磁针给了旅人一条固定线，其余方向都由它量出。

senses.title: The drawing tool
senses.definition: a tool with two legs used for drawing circles
senses.definitionCN: 用来画圆的两脚工具
senses.example: He drew a perfect circle with a compass.
senses.exampleCN: 他用圆规画了一个完美的圆。
senses.why: Both meanings turn on measuring a circle or a round world, so they share one name.
senses.whyCN: 两个义项都围绕测量圆或圆形世界，所以共用一个名字。

senses.title: The range or scope
senses.definition: the limit or range of something
senses.definitionCN: 某事物的限度或范围
senses.example: Such a journey lies beyond the compass of one summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这样的旅程超出了一个夏天的范围。
senses.why: A compass marks how far a circle reaches, so it came to mean any reach or limit.
senses.whyCN: 罗盘标出圆能伸到多远，于是引申为任何范围或限度。

intro.en: Compass comes from Latin com, together, and passus, a step, and first meant to pace out a circle of ground.
intro.cn: compass 来自拉丁语 com（一起）与 passus（一步），本义是按步量出一圈地面。

items.en: Passus was the length of one step.
items.cn: passus 指一步的长度。

items.en: Compassare meant to measure a space by walking round it.
items.cn: compassare 意为绕着走一圈来量一块地方。

items.en: Old French compasser kept the sense of going round.
items.cn: 古法语 compasser 保留了绕行一圈的意思。

items.en: English compass first named a circuit or a boundary.
items.cn: 英语 compass 最初指一圈或一条边界。

items.en: It moved to the needle for direction, the tool for circles and any scope.
items.cn: 后来它转向指方向的磁针、画圆的工具以及任何范围。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words with a similar sound or shape, and the meaning group names other words for direction, range and guidance.
note.cn: 形近组收的是读音或形状相近的词，近义组列出其他表示方向、范围与指引的词。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a needle settling on north, then move to the tool that draws circles and to any reach or limit.

normal.en: Com- is together and pass means step, so a compass measures a walk in a circle.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，pass 是步子，所以 compass 量的是绕一圈的路。

normal.en: One needle, one fixed north: that is why a compass calms a lost walker.
normal.cn: 一根磁针，一个固定的北方：所以罗盘能让迷路的人安心。

normal.en: Two legs and a point draw a perfect circle.
normal.cn: 两条腿加一个尖点，就能画出完美的圆。

normal.en: The compass of a book is the range it covers.
normal.cn: 一本书的 compass 就是它覆盖的范围。

normal.en: En- plus compass gives encompass, to go all the way round.
normal.cn: en- 加 compass 得到 encompass，意为整个围起来。

abstract.cn: 想象磁针抖了几下，然后定在北方不动。

abstract.en: Picture a metal point pressed into paper, a circle opening out.
abstract.cn: 想象金属尖压进纸里，一个圆慢慢张开。

abstract.en: Picture a fence that marks how far the land goes.
abstract.cn: 想象一道篱笆，标出土地延伸到哪里。

examples.cn: 指南针的指针稳稳地指向北方。

examples.cn: 用圆规和铅笔画这个圆。

examples.en: That subject lies beyond the compass of this book.
examples.cn: 那个题目超出了本书的范围。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 compass 记成 com（一起）加 pass（步）：一起量步、绕行一圈，圆盘定方向，两脚画圆，也都量出范围。

root: 源自拉丁语 com（一起）与 passus（步），本义是按步量地、绕行一圈，后指量圆的工具与指示方向的罗盘，再引申为范围。

branches.en: Finding north is the sense travellers cling to.

branches.en: The drawing tool keeps the old idea of a measured circle.
branches.cn: 画圆工具保留了量出一个圆的古老想法。

branches.cn: 两个义项都出自同一个动作：量出一块圆的范围。

intro.en: Compass is built on Latin com, together, plus passus, a step.

items.meaning: one of the main directions on a compass

items.meaning: the printed star of directions on a map

definition_en: a strong feeling of sympathy for someone who is suffering, together with a wish to help
core_image: 看见别人蹲在雨里发抖，自己也不由得停下脚步
scene: 同事的母亲住院，她把热汤放在对方桌上没有多问。Her compassion showed in small, quiet acts.
sceneCN: 这里 compassion 指「同情；关怀」（第 1 个义项：对他人苦难的体恤）；句意是她的关怀体现在细小而安静的举动里。

senses.title: Sympathy for suffering
senses.definition: a feeling of pity for someone who is suffering
senses.definitionCN: 对正在受苦之人的怜惜之情
senses.example: She felt deep compassion for the lost child.
senses.exampleCN: 她对那个走失的孩子深感同情。
senses.why: Com- means with, and the root means to suffer, so compassion is suffering alongside.
senses.whyCN: com- 表示与…同在，词根表示受苦，所以 compassion 是与他人一同受苦。

senses.title: Sympathy that moves you to help
senses.definition: sympathy strong enough to make you want to act
senses.definitionCN: 强到让你想要行动的同情
senses.example: The nurse treated every patient with compassion.
senses.exampleCN: 这位护士以关怀之心对待每位病人。
senses.why: Feeling alone is passive; compassion carries the push to ease another's pain.
senses.whyCN: 单纯的感觉是被动的，compassion 带着减轻他人痛苦的推力。

intro.en: Compassion comes from Latin com, with, and pati, to suffer: to feel pain together with someone.
intro.cn: compassion 来自拉丁语 com（与…同在）与 pati（受苦）：与某人一同感到疼痛。

items.en: Pati meant to suffer or to endure.
items.cn: pati 意为受苦或忍受。

items.en: Compassio meant suffering together with another person.
items.cn: compassio 意为与另一个人一同受苦。

items.en: The church used compassio for shared grief.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语教会用 compassio 指共同承担的悲伤。

items.en: Old French compassion softened it into tender pity.
items.cn: 古法语 compassion 把它软化为温柔的怜惜。

items.en: English compassion joined pity with the wish to help.
items.cn: 英语 compassion 把怜惜与想帮忙的心愿合在一起。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words that echo the spelling of compassion, and the meaning group separates sympathy, pity and empathy.
note.cn: 形近组收的是拼写与 compassion 相近的词，近义组分辨同情、怜悯与共情。

able to work well together

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with shared suffering, then move to the push to help and to the quiet shape it takes.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从共同受苦开始，再走到想帮忙的推力以及它安静的样子。

normal.en: Com- is with and passion here means suffering, so compassion is feeling with someone.
normal.cn: com- 是与…同在，这里的 passion 指受苦，所以 compassion 就是与人同感。

normal.en: Pity looks down; compassion sits down beside you.
normal.cn: pity 是俯视，compassion 是在你身边坐下。

normal.en: Compassion is not softness; it often means doing the hard thing.
normal.cn: compassion 不是软弱，它常常意味着去做难做的事。

normal.en: The adjective is compassionate, the adverb compassionately.
normal.cn: 形容词是 compassionate，副词是 compassionately。

normal.en: Compassion fatigue is what carers feel after too many nights.
normal.cn: 同情疲劳是照护者熬过太多夜晚后的感受。

abstract.cn: 想象一个陌生人把伞举到已经淋湿的人头上。

abstract.en: Picture a hand placed quietly on a shaking shoulder.
abstract.cn: 想象一只手静静放在发抖的肩上。

abstract.en: Picture hot soup left on a desk with no note.
abstract.cn: 想象一碗热汤放在桌上，没有留字条。

examples.en: Her compassion for the stray dogs was well known.
examples.cn: 她对流浪狗的同情是出了名的。

examples.en: He spoke with compassion rather than blame.
examples.cn: 他说话带着同情，而不是责备。

examples.en: Compassion costs nothing but means everything.
examples.cn: 同情不花一文，却意义重大。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 compassion 记成 com（一起）加 passion（受苦）：与人一起受苦，就是同情。

root: 源自拉丁语 com（一起）与 pati（受苦），本义是与他人一同受苦，后引申为同情、怜悯与愿意相助的关怀。

sensesIntro.en: From feeling another's pain, to being moved to relieve it.
sensesIntro.cn: 从感受他人的痛苦，到被推动去减轻它。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone stopping in the rain because a stranger is shivering.
core.cn: 核心意象：看见别人蹲在雨里发抖，自己也不由得停下脚步。

branches.en: Feeling the pain is the root sense of compassion.
branches.cn: 感受到那份痛，是 compassion 的词根义。

branches.en: Compassion that stays a feeling has not finished its work.
branches.cn: 只停在感受上的 compassion，还没有做完它的事。

branches.en: Feeling and acting are one movement in this word.
branches.cn: 在这个词里，感受与行动是同一个动作。

branches.en: The Latin root already joined the pain with the shared response.
branches.cn: 拉丁词根早已把痛与共同的回应连在一起。

branches.en: Care shows best in small acts that ask for no thanks.
branches.cn: 关怀最常显现在不讨谢意的小事上。

intro.en: Compassion is built on Latin com, with, plus the suffering base pati.

latinIntro.en: The same patient root gives patient and patience, both about enduring.
latinIntro.cn: 同一个表示忍受的词根还给出 patient 与 patience，两者都与忍耐有关。

definition_en: to force someone to do something, or to make something happen inevitably
core_image: 一只手按在背上，把人往前推了一步
scene: 暴雨越下越大，司机只好把车停到路边。The storm compelled them to stop and wait.
sceneCN: 这里 compel 指「迫使」（第 1 个义项：让人不得不做）；句意是暴雨迫使他们停下来等。

derivatives.zh: 令人信服的；引人入胜的

senses.title: To force a person
senses.definition: to make someone do something by force or pressure
senses.definitionCN: 用力量或压力使某人做某事
senses.example: Illness compelled her to leave the job.
senses.exampleCN: 疾病迫使她辞去工作。
senses.why: The Latin base means to drive, so the word carries a push from behind.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁词基意为驱赶，所以这个词带有从背后推的力量。

senses.title: To make something unavoidable
senses.definition: to make an event or feeling impossible to avoid
senses.definitionCN: 使某件事或某种感受无法避免
senses.example: The story compels attention from the first line.
senses.exampleCN: 这个故事从第一行就让人不得不注意。
senses.why: Pressure can fall on things as well as people, and then compel means to demand.
senses.whyCN: 压力也会落在事物上，此时 compel 意为强烈要求。

intro.en: Compel comes from Latin compellere, to drive together, from com, together, and pellere, to push.
intro.cn: compel 来自拉丁语 compellere，意为往一处赶，由 com（一起）与 pellere（推动）构成。

items.en: Pellere meant to push, to drive or to strike.
items.cn: pellere 意为推、赶或击打。

items.en: Compellere meant to drive someone into a corner.
items.cn: compellere 意为把人逼到角落。

items.en: Roman law used it for forcing a person to appear.
items.cn: 罗马法律用它表示强制某人到场。

items.en: Old French compeller kept the sense of pressure.
items.cn: 古法语 compeller 保留了压力的含义。

items.en: English compel widened to any strong necessity.
items.cn: 英语 compel 扩展到任何强烈的必然。

note.en: The look-alike group holds short verbs close in shape to compel, and the meaning group ranks the verbs of pressure from force to urging.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 compel 形状相近的短动词，近义组按从强迫到敦促排出表示压力的动词。

core_image: 天平一端缺了砝码，另一端补上同等重量
scene: 工地摔伤之后，公司按合同支付了一笔款项。The worker received compensation for his injury.
sceneCN: 这里 compensation 指「赔偿金」（第 1 个义项：为损失支付的补偿）；句意是这名工人因受伤得到了赔偿。

senses.title: Payment for loss
senses.definition: money paid to someone because they have suffered loss or injury
senses.definitionCN: 因遭受损失或伤害而支付给某人的钱
senses.example: The family received compensation for the damaged house.
senses.exampleCN: 这家人因房屋受损获得了赔偿。
senses.why: When loss cannot be undone, money is offered to make the balance level again.
senses.whyCN: 损失无法挽回时，用钱把天平重新找平。

senses.title: Pay for work
senses.definition: the money and benefits paid for a job
senses.definitionCN: 为一份工作支付的金钱与福利
senses.example: The job offers good compensation and free meals.
senses.exampleCN: 这份工作报酬不错，还管饭。
senses.why: Work is also a cost to the worker, so pay is framed as making it even.
senses.whyCN: 工作对劳动者也是付出，因此工资被说成把账找平。

senses.title: Something that balances a flaw
senses.definition: something good that balances a disadvantage
senses.definitionCN: 用来抵消缺点的好处
senses.example: The quiet garden is compensation for the small rooms.
senses.exampleCN: 安静的花园弥补了房间狭小。
senses.why: Not all debts are paid in money; a good point can answer a bad one.
senses.whyCN: 并非所有亏欠都用钱偿还，一个优点也能抵消一个缺点。

intro.en: Compensation comes from Latin compensare, to weigh one thing against another until they balance.
intro.cn: compensation 来自拉丁语 compensare，意为把一物与另一物相称，直到两边平衡。

items.en: Pensare meant to weigh or to pay out.
items.cn: pensare 意为称重或称量支付。

items.en: Compensare meant to balance one sum against another.
items.cn: compensare 意为用一笔抵另一笔，使两边相平。

items.en: Compensatio named the settling of that balance.
items.cn: compensatio 指把这笔账找平。

items.en: Old French compensation kept the bookkeeping sense.
items.cn: 古法语 compensation 保留了记账式的含义。

items.en: English compensation widened to injury, pay and any offset.
items.cn: 英语 compensation 扩展到伤害赔偿、薪酬与任何抵消。

note.en: The look-alike group holds related but different -tion nouns, and the meaning group separates repayment, damages and salary.
note.cn: 形近组收的是相关却不同的名词，近义组分辨偿还款项、损害赔偿金与薪水。

entries.definition: to pay someone for a loss
a contest or a rivalry
the way parts are put together
money paid back to someone
money a court orders for harm done
fixed pay for a job

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a short weight on one pan, then move to pay for work and to a good point that answers a bad one.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一端缺了砝码开始，再走到工作的报酬以及用一个优点抵消一个缺点。

normal.en: Com- is together and pens means weigh, so compensation is the weight added to level the pans.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，pens 是称重，compensation 就是补上去把那两盘称平的重量。

normal.en: Compensate is the verb and compensation the noun of the same settling.
normal.cn: compensate 是动词，compensation 是同一次找平的名词。

normal.en: You claim compensation, and a firm pays it.
normal.cn: 你提出索赔，公司支付赔偿。

normal.en: A compensation package is pay plus holidays plus insurance.
normal.cn: 薪酬方案是工资加假期再加保险。

normal.en: The view from the top floor is compensation for the stairs.
normal.cn: 顶楼的风景，是对爬楼梯的弥补。

abstract.en: Picture one pan of a balance rising, then a hand adding weight.
abstract.cn: 想象天平一端翘起，一只手往上加砝码。

abstract.en: Picture a pay slip folded inside a white envelope.
abstract.cn: 想象一张工资条折好放在白信封里。

abstract.en: Picture a small balcony that makes a tiny flat worth living in.
abstract.cn: 想象一个小阳台，让一间小公寓值得住下去。

examples.en: She asked for compensation after the delay.
examples.cn: 延误之后她要求赔偿。

examples.en: The company paid compensation to the farmers.
examples.cn: 公司向农民支付了赔偿。

examples.en: Working from home is some compensation for the long hours.
examples.cn: 在家办公算是对长时间工作的一种弥补。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 compensation 记成 com（一起）加 pens（称重）加 ation：把两边的重量称平，就是补偿。

root: 源自拉丁语 compensare，com- 表示一起，pensare 表示称重，本义是把两边称平，后引申为赔偿金、报酬与弥补。

sensesIntro.en: From money that levels a loss, to pay for work, and finally to any good point that answers a bad one.
sensesIntro.cn: 从把损失称平的赔偿，到工作的报酬，最后到任何抵消缺点的好处。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: one pan of a balance is short of weight, so a matching weight is added.
core.cn: 核心意象：天平一端缺了砝码，另一端补上同等重量。

branches.en: Money for injury is the clearest modern sense.
branches.cn: 为伤害付钱是现代最清楚的义项。

branches.en: Pay treats work as a cost that must be made even.
branches.cn: 工资把劳动看作一份需要找平的付出。

branches.en: Not every debt is money, yet every debt wants balance.
branches.cn: 并非每笔亏欠都是钱，但每笔亏欠都想要平衡。

branches.en: Both are settled on the same old balance.
branches.cn: 两者都在同一台古老的天平上了结。

branches.en: A good point and a sum of money both answer a loss.
branches.cn: 一个优点与一笔钱，都在回应一份损失。

intro.en: Compensation joins the verb compensate with the noun ending -ation.
intro.cn: compensation 由动词 compensate 加名词后缀 -ation 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin pensare, to weigh, also gives us pensive and pension.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 pensare（称重）还给出了 pensive 与 pension 这样的词。

items.example: The small compensations made the job bearable.
items.exampleCN: 那些小小的补偿让这份工作还过得去。

items.meaning: to make up for a loss
items.example: Nothing can compensate for the lost time.
items.exampleCN: 什么也弥补不了失去的时间。

items.example: Good coffee compensates for a poor view.
items.exampleCN: 好咖啡弥补了视野不佳。
工人们得到了全额补偿。

items.example: He worked late as a compensating effort.

items.exampleCN: 法院判给了补偿性款项。

items.meaning: a person or device that compensates
items.example: The device acts as a heat compensator.
items.exampleCN: 这个装置起热补偿作用。

items.example: The loss is compensable under the law.
items.exampleCN: 这种损失依法可获补偿。

definition_en: to try to be more successful than others, or to take part in a contest
core_image: 两名跑者在同一条跑道上并排冲向终点
scene: 小店老板把价格压到最低，仍担心对面新开的店。Small shops find it hard to compete with big chains.
sceneCN: 这里 compete 指「竞争」（第 1 个义项：争取胜过他人）；句意是小店很难与大型连锁店竞争。

senses.title: To strive against others
senses.definition: to try hard to gain something that others also want
senses.definitionCN: 努力争取别人也想要的东西
senses.example: Five firms competed for the same contract.
senses.exampleCN: 五家公司争夺同一份合同。
senses.why: Two parties reaching for one prize is the oldest shape of the word.
senses.whyCN: 两方伸手去够同一个奖赏，是这个词最古老的样子。

senses.title: To take part in a contest
senses.definition: to take part in a race, match or game
senses.definitionCN: 参加赛跑、比赛或竞技
senses.example: She competed in three events at the games.
senses.exampleCN: 她在运动会上参加了三个项目。
senses.why: From striving, the word narrows to a formal contest with rules and a finish.
senses.whyCN: 从努力争取，这个词收窄到有规则与终点的正式比赛。

intro.en: Compete comes from Latin competere, to seek something together, from com, together, and petere, to seek.
intro.cn: compete 来自拉丁语 competere，意为一起追求某物，由 com（一起）与 petere（追求）构成。

items.en: Petere meant to seek, to aim at or to ask for.
items.cn: petere 意为寻求、瞄准或请求。

items.en: Competere meant to seek the same thing as another.
items.cn: competere 意为与别人追求同一样东西。

items.en: It also meant to be fit for a task or an office.
items.cn: 它也指适合某项任务或职位。

items.en: Old French competir narrowed it to rivalry.
items.cn: 古法语 competir 把词义收窄到争胜。

items.en: English compete covered both trade rivals and sports.
items.cn: 英语 compete 同时覆盖商业对手与体育竞技。

note.en: The look-alike group holds verbs one letter away from compete, and the meaning group ranks the verbs of rivalry.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 compete 只差一个字母的动词，近义组排出表示争胜的动词。

entries.definition: to finish something
to obey a rule or request
to calculate a result
to compete for a prize
to be as good as another
to compete for something

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with one prize and many hands, then move to shops that cut prices and to races with rules.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从一个奖赏与许多只手开始，再走到压价的小店与有规则的赛跑。

normal.en: Com- is together and pete means seek, so compete is to seek the same thing together.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，pete 是寻求，compete 就是一起去求同一样东西。

normal.en: Compete with a rival, compete for a prize, compete in a race.
normal.cn: 与对手 compete with，为奖品 compete for，在赛场上 compete in。

normal.en: The noun is competition, the person is a competitor.
normal.cn: 名词是 competition，人就是 competitor。

normal.en: Competitive prices keep a small shop alive.
normal.cn: 有竞争力的价格让小店的活路得以延续。

normal.en: You cannot compete if you never enter.
normal.cn: 不进场，就谈不上竞争。

abstract.en: Picture two hands reaching for one last ticket.
abstract.cn: 想象两只手同时伸向最后一张票。

abstract.en: Picture two shops posting new prices in one morning.
abstract.cn: 想象两家店在同一个早上挂出新价签。

abstract.en: Picture five swimmers bent on the blocks, waiting for the whistle.
abstract.cn: 想象五名泳者伏在出发台上，等着哨声。

examples.en: Small firms must compete on quality.
examples.cn: 小公司必须在质量上竞争。

examples.en: He competed against runners from ten countries.
examples.cn: 他与来自十个国家的跑者同场竞技。

examples.en: Two cities competed for the new factory.
examples.cn: 两座城市争夺这家新工厂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 compete 记成 com（一起）加 pete（寻求）：大家一起伸手去求同一个东西，就是竞争。

root: 源自拉丁语 competere，com- 表示一起，petere 表示追求，本义是一起追求同一个目标，后引申为竞争与参赛。

sensesIntro.en: From striving for one prize, to entering a contest with rules.
sensesIntro.cn: 从为同一个奖赏而努力，到参加有规则的比赛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two runners side by side on one track, driving toward the same line.
core.cn: 核心意象：两名跑者在同一条跑道上并排冲向终点。

branches.en: Striving for a shared goal is the root sense.
branches.cn: 为共同目标而努力，是这个词的词根义。

branches.en: A contest is the same striving with rules added.
branches.cn: 比赛就是同样的争胜加上了规则。

branches.en: Shops and runners both want to finish first.
branches.cn: 商店与跑者都想第一个到达。

branches.en: The word needs a rival; nobody competes alone.
branches.cn: 这个词需要一个对手；没有人独自竞争。

branches.en: To compete in an event is to accept its rules.
branches.cn: 参加一项比赛，就是接受它的规则。

intro.en: Compete is built on Latin com, together, plus petere, to seek.
intro.cn: compete 由拉丁语 com（一起）加 petere（追求）构成。

latinIntro.en: The seeking base pet- also appears in appetite and petition.
latinIntro.cn: 表示追求的词基 pet- 也出现在 appetite 与 petition 里。

items.example: The team competed in three cities.
items.exampleCN: 这支队伍在三座城市参赛。

items.example: The two are competing for the same buyers.
items.exampleCN: 两家在争夺同一批买家。

items.meaning: a person or firm you compete with
items.example: Our main competitor cut its prices.
items.exampleCN: 我们的主要对手降价了。
训练提高了队伍的竞争力。

definition_zh: 有能力的；胜任的；合格的
definition_en: having enough skill or knowledge to do something properly
core_image: 工匠一手扶住木料，一手稳稳下刀，不多不少
scene: 新来的电工查了一遍线路，十几分钟就排除了故障。She is competent enough to handle the job alone.
sceneCN: 这里 competent 指「有能力的；胜任的」（第 1 个义项：具备足够本领）；句意是她足以独立处理这项工作。

pos.zh: 有能力的；胜任的；合格的

senses.title: Skilled enough to do the job
senses.definition: having enough skill or knowledge for a task
senses.definitionCN: 具备完成任务所需的技能或知识
senses.example: She is a competent driver on mountain roads.
senses.exampleCN: 她在山路上是个称职的司机。
senses.why: The word asks one quiet question: can this person carry the task safely?
senses.whyCN: 这个词只问一个朴素的问题：这人能把事稳妥地担起来吗。

senses.title: Acceptable but not outstanding
senses.definition: good enough to be accepted, though not excellent
senses.definitionCN: 足以被接受，但算不上出色
senses.example: The report is competent but never exciting.
senses.exampleCN: 这份报告合格，却谈不上精彩。
senses.why: Once a bar is set, meeting it exactly can sound like faint praise.
senses.whyCN: 一旦有了及格线，刚刚够到就会带一点勉强的称赞。

intro.en: Competent comes from Latin competere, which also meant to be fit for a task.
intro.cn: competent 来自拉丁语 competere，这个词也有「适合某项任务」的意思。

items.en: Petere meant to seek or to aim at.
items.cn: petere 意为追求或瞄准。

items.en: Competere could mean to be suitable for something.
items.cn: competere 可以表示适合某事。

items.en: Competens described a person equal to a duty.
items.cn: competens 描述能担起职责的人。

items.en: Old French competent kept the sense of being fit.
items.cn: 古法语 competent 保留了「合适、称职」的含义。

items.en: English competent settled into skill and legal fitness.
items.cn: 英语 competent 落在技能与法律资格两方面。

note.en: The look-alike group holds members of the compete family, and the meaning group ranks capable, qualified and merely skilled.
note.cn: 形近组收的是 compete 家族的成员，近义组分辨有能力的、合格的和只是熟练的。

to strive against others
able to do something well

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a steady knife, then move to the standard a task sets and to the mild praise of just meeting it.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从稳稳的一刀开始，再走到任务设定的标准以及刚刚够格时那点温和的称赞。

normal.en: Competent shares a root with compete: you are fit for the task at hand.
normal.cn: competent 与 compete 同根：你对眼前这件事是够格的。

normal.en: Competent is about the bar, not about brilliance.
normal.cn: competent 说的是及格线，而不是出众。

normal.en: The noun is competence, and its opposite is incompetence.
normal.cn: 名词是 competence，反面就是 incompetence。

normal.en: A competent cook never burns the rice.
normal.cn: 一个称职的厨子不会把米饭烧糊。

normal.en: Competent at a task means you can be trusted with it.
normal.cn: competent at 一项任务，意味着这件事可以交给你。

abstract.en: Picture a knife following a pencilled line without slipping.
abstract.cn: 想象一刀顺着铅笔线走，没有偏。

abstract.en: Picture a driver checking the mirror before changing lanes.
abstract.cn: 想象司机变道前先看一眼后视镜。

abstract.en: Picture a bar just touched by a jumper's hand.
abstract.cn: 想象跳高者的手刚好碰到横杆。

examples.en: A competent mechanic can find the fault quickly.
examples.cn: 一个有能力的技工能很快找出故障。

examples.en: The team is competent at handling complaints.
examples.cn: 这个团队处理投诉很在行。

examples.en: Her work is competent rather than brilliant.
examples.cn: 她的工作合格，但算不上出色。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 competent 记成 com（一起）加 pet（追求）加 ent：追得上任务要求的人，就是有能力的。

root: 源自拉丁语 competere，本义是「足以相称、合乎要求」，后指具备足够本领的、胜任的。

sensesIntro.en: From having the skill a task demands, to just meeting the bar and no more.
sensesIntro.cn: 从拥有任务所需的技能，到刚好够上及格线。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a carpenter whose knife follows the line without slipping.
core.cn: 核心意象：工匠一手扶住木料，一手稳稳下刀，不多不少。

branches.en: Being fit for the task is the practical core.
branches.cn: 足以胜任任务是这个词务实的核心。

branches.en: Meeting the bar exactly can sound like faint praise.
branches.cn: 刚好够到及格线，听起来就像淡淡的称赞。

branches.en: Both senses measure a person against a standard.
branches.cn: 两个义项都是拿一个人去对照一个标准。

branches.en: Trust grows when skill can be relied on.
branches.cn: 本领可靠，信任才会生长。

branches.en: The second sense warns against stopping at good enough.
branches.cn: 第二个义项提醒人别停在「够用」上。

intro.en: Competent takes the Latin base compet- and the adjective ending -ent.
intro.cn: competent 由拉丁词基 compet- 加形容词后缀 -ent 构成。

latinIntro.en: The same base yields competence, competent and competition.
latinIntro.cn: 同一个词基产出 competence、competent 与 competition。

items.meaning: the ability to do something well
items.example: Her competence reassured the whole team.
items.exampleCN: 她的能力让整个团队安心。

items.meaning: a specific skill needed for a job
items.example: The job lists five core competencies.
items.exampleCN: 这份工作列出五项核心能力。

items.meaning: in a skilled and reliable way
items.exampleCN: 她称职地处理了这个案子。

items.meaning: not skilled enough for a task

items.exampleCN: 不称职的飞行员是一种危险。

items.meaning: lack of skill for a task

items.example: Managers need both technical and social competencies.
items.exampleCN: 管理者既需要技术专长，也需要社交能力。

definition_en: an event in which people try to win, or the rivalry between people or firms who want the same thing
core_image: 几条船挤在同一条起跑线上，桨叶同时入水
scene: 报名表贴出三天，走廊里已经挤满了准备参赛的学生。The competition attracted students from twenty schools.
sceneCN: 这里 competition 指「比赛」（第 1 个义项：争夺名次的活动）；句意是这场比赛吸引了二十所学校的学生。

senses.title: A contest
senses.definition: an event in which people try to win a prize
senses.definitionCN: 人们争夺奖项的活动
senses.example: She won the writing competition at school.
senses.exampleCN: 她在学校作文比赛中获奖。
senses.why: A fixed event with rules turns rivalry into something you can watch and score.
senses.whyCN: 有规则、有场地的活动，把争胜变成看得见、可评分的事。

senses.title: Rivalry between people or firms
senses.definition: the struggle between people or companies for the same aim
senses.definitionCN: 人或公司为同一目标而进行的争夺
senses.example: Price competition keeps the market healthy.
senses.exampleCN: 价格竞争让市场保持健康。
senses.why: The same striving continues without a referee, in shops and offices.
senses.whyCN: 同样的争胜在没有裁判的商店与办公室里继续。

senses.title: The rivals themselves
senses.definition: the people or firms you are trying to beat
senses.definitionCN: 你想要胜过的那些人或公司
senses.example: The competition has cut its prices again.
senses.exampleCN: 竞争对手又降价了。
senses.why: By a small shift, the contest comes to mean the other side in it.
senses.whyCN: 词义轻轻一转，比赛就指比赛里的对方。

intro.en: Competition comes from Latin competitio, the noun of competere, to seek the same thing together.
intro.cn: competition 来自拉丁语 competitio，是 competere（一起追求同一目标）的名词形式。

items.en: Competere meant to seek the same prize as another.
items.cn: competere 意为与别人追求同一个奖赏。

items.en: Competitio named the shared striving itself.
items.cn: competitio 指这种共同的争求本身。

items.en: It also described a legal claim between two parties.
items.cn: 它也描述两方之间的法律争讼。

items.en: Old French competition narrowed to contests and trade.
items.cn: 古法语 competition 收窄到比赛与商业。

items.en: English competition covered sport, markets and rival firms.
items.cn: 英语 competition 覆盖体育、市场与对手公司。

note.en: The look-alike group holds other -tion nouns easily confused with competition, and the meaning group separates a contest, a rivalry and a match.

entries.definition: the way parts are arranged
the act of finishing
payment for a loss
an event where people try to win
strong competition between equals
a game between two sides

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with boats on one line, then move to the everyday struggle and to the rivals on the other side.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从同一条起跑线上的船开始，再走到日常的争夺以及对面的对手。

normal.en: Competition is the noun behind compete: it names the whole scene.
normal.cn: competition 是 compete 背后的名词：它给整个场面命名。

normal.en: Enter a competition, win a competition, but feel competition in a market.
normal.cn: 可以说参加比赛、赢得比赛，也会在市场里感受到竞争。

normal.en: Fierce competition is the phrase shops use when prices fall.
normal.cn: 降价时商家会说竞争激烈，用的就是 fierce competition。

normal.en: The competition can also be the other team, not the event.
normal.cn: the competition 也可以指对方队伍，而不是那场活动。

normal.en: A competitor is one person; competition is the whole field.
normal.cn: competitor 是一个人，competition 是整个赛场。

abstract.en: Picture five oars hitting the water at the same second.
abstract.cn: 想象五支桨在同一秒入水。

abstract.en: Picture two price boards changing in the same street.
abstract.cn: 想象同一条街上两块价目牌先后更换。

abstract.en: Picture a judge holding a list of names and a stopwatch.
abstract.cn: 想象裁判拿着名单和秒表。

examples.en: The design competition drew over a hundred entries.
examples.cn: 这次设计比赛收到一百多件作品。

examples.en: Fierce competition forced the shop to close.
examples.cn: 激烈的竞争迫使这家店关门。

examples.en: Our competition launched a cheaper model.
examples.cn: 我们的竞争对手推出了一款更便宜的型号。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 competition 记成 com（一起）加 pet（追求）加 ition：一群人一起追同一个奖品，就是竞争与比赛。

root: 源自拉丁语 competitio，由 competere（一起追求）加名词后缀而来，本义是共同争求同一目标，后指比赛、竞争与对手。

sensesIntro.en: From a scored contest, to the everyday struggle, and finally to the rivals in it.
sensesIntro.cn: 从计分的比赛，到日常的争夺，最后到争夺中的对手。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: several boats pressed against one starting line, oars entering the water at once.
core.cn: 核心意象：几条船挤在同一条起跑线上，桨叶同时入水。

branches.en: The scored event is the clearest sense of competition.
branches.cn: 计分的赛事是 competition 最清楚的义项。

branches.en: Without rules, the same striving becomes market rivalry.
branches.cn: 没有规则时，同样的争胜就成了市场竞争。

branches.en: The contest can stand for the other side in it.
branches.cn: 比赛可以代指比赛里的另一方。

branches.en: Both are one prize chased by many hands.
branches.cn: 两者都是许多只手去追同一个奖赏。

branches.en: In business the rivals are the competition.
branches.cn: 在生意里，对手就是 the competition。

intro.en: Competition joins the verb compete with the noun ending -ition.
intro.cn: competition 由动词 compete 加名词后缀 -ition 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin petere, to seek, is the small engine inside the whole family.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 petere（追求）是整个词族内部的小引擎。

items.example: The school holds three competitions a year.
items.exampleCN: 学校每年举办三场比赛。

items.example: They compete for the same buyers.
Two competing plans were on the table.
items.exampleCN: 桌上有两个相互竞争方案。

items.meaning: eager to win or able to win
items.example: The firm stays competitive by cutting costs.
items.exampleCN: 这家公司靠削减成本保持竞争力。
每位参赛者都戴着一个号码。
这个指数衡量经济竞争力。

definition_zh: 竞争的；有竞争力的；争强好胜的
definition_en: relating to competition, cheap enough to beat rivals, or wanting very much to win
core_image: 跑道上的人侧头盯着旁边的选手，脚下加快
scene: 招聘会上，同一个岗位前排了很长的队。The job market is highly competitive this year.
sceneCN: 这里 competitive 指「竞争激烈的」（第 1 个义项：充满竞争的）；句意是今年的就业市场竞争十分激烈。

pos.zh: 竞争的；有竞争力的；争强好胜的

senses.title: Full of competition
senses.definition: involving people or firms trying to win
senses.definitionCN: 涉及人或公司争胜的
senses.example: The software market is fiercely competitive.
senses.exampleCN: 软件市场竞争激烈。
senses.why: An adjective from competition simply describes the arena where rivals meet.
senses.whyCN: 由 competition 来的形容词，只描述对手相遇的场地。

senses.title: Good enough to win
senses.definition: low or good enough to beat what rivals offer
senses.definitionCN: 低或好到能胜过对手的
senses.example: They offered a competitive price on the laptop.
senses.exampleCN: 他们给这台笔记本报了个有竞争力的价格。
senses.why: From describing the contest, the word moves to describing a winning position in it.
senses.whyCN: 从描述比赛，转为描述在比赛中占优的位置。

senses.title: Eager to win
senses.definition: wanting very much to beat others
senses.definitionCN: 非常想胜过别人的
senses.example: He is too competitive to enjoy a friendly game.
senses.exampleCN: 他太争强好胜，玩不成轻松的游戏。
senses.why: The same drive can be praised in a market and frowned on at a dinner table.
senses.whyCN: 同一种冲劲在市场里被称赞，在饭桌上却被皱眉。

intro.en: Competitive adds the ending -ive to the Latin base of compete, naming what belongs to rivalry.
intro.cn: competitive 在 compete 的拉丁词基上加后缀 -ive，表示属于争胜的东西。

items.en: Competere meant to seek the same thing as another.
items.cn: competere 意为与别人追求同一样东西。

items.en: Competitivus described things that belonged to a contest.
items.cn: competitivus 描述属于争胜的事物。

items.en: English competitive first described sports and exams.
items.cn: 英语 competitive 最初描述体育与考试。

items.en: Trade writers applied it to prices and markets.
items.cn: 商业作者把它用到价格与市场上。

items.en: It now also describes a person who hates to lose.
items.cn: 如今它也用来形容输不起的人。

note.en: The look-alike group holds other compete forms, and the meaning group separates ambitious drive from an aggressive manner and a cheap price.
note.cn: 形近组收的是 compete 的其他形式，近义组分辨雄心、强势作风与低廉价格。

a contest or a rivalry

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a sideways glance at a rival, then move to a price that wins and to a temper that must win.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从斜眼看向对手开始，再走到能取胜的价格与非赢不可的性子。

normal.en: Competitive carries -ive, so it describes a field full of competing.
normal.cn: competitive 带着 -ive，所以它描述一个充满竞争的场域。

normal.en: A competitive price is a price that competes and wins.
normal.cn: 有竞争力的价格，就是能参与竞争并胜出的价格。

normal.en: A competitive person keeps score even in the garden.
normal.cn: 好胜的人连在花园里也要计分。

normal.en: Competitive is the adjective, competitiveness the quality.
normal.cn: competitive 是形容词，competitiveness 是那种性质。

normal.en: The phrase competitive edge is the small gap that wins.
normal.cn: competitive edge 就是决定胜负的那一点点差距。

abstract.en: Picture a runner half a step ahead, breathing hard.
abstract.cn: 想象跑者领先半步，喘着粗气。

abstract.en: Picture two price tags, one lower by a few coins.
abstract.cn: 想象两个价签，一个低了几枚硬币。

abstract.en: Picture a chess player refusing a draw.
abstract.cn: 想象棋手拒绝和棋。

examples.en: Small shops struggle to stay competitive.
examples.cn: 小店很难保持竞争力。

examples.en: She has a competitive streak that shows in every game.
examples.cn: 她有一股好胜劲，每场游戏都看得出来。

examples.en: The hotel offers competitive rates in winter.
examples.cn: 这家酒店冬季价格很有竞争力。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 competitive 记成 compete（竞争）加 itive：带着竞争劲儿的，就是有竞争力的、好胜的。

root: 源自拉丁语 competere（一起追求），加形容词后缀 -ive，本义属于竞争的，后引申为有竞争力的与争强好胜的。

sensesIntro.en: From the arena itself, to a winning price, and finally to the temper that must win.
sensesIntro.cn: 从场地本身，到能取胜的价格，最后到非赢不可的性子。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a runner glancing sideways at a rival, feet quickening.
core.cn: 核心意象：跑道上的人侧头盯着旁边的选手，脚下加快。

branches.en: The first sense simply describes a crowded field.
branches.cn: 第一个义项只是描述一个人挤人的场域。

branches.en: A price earns the word when it can beat the shop next door.
branches.cn: 价格能压过隔壁店时，才配得上这个词。

branches.en: The same drive turns inward and becomes a temperament.
branches.cn: 同一种冲劲转向内里，就成了一种性情。

branches.en: A market is competitive because its offers compete.
branches.cn: 市场之所以叫竞争性，是因为其中的报价在相互竞争。

branches.en: Winning prices and winning tempers share one source.
branches.cn: 取胜的价格与好胜的性子同出一源。

intro.en: Competitive takes the Latin base compet- and the adjective ending -itive.
intro.cn: competitive 由拉丁词基 compet- 加形容词后缀 -itive 构成。

latinIntro.en: Every form in this family carries the seeking base pet-.
latinIntro.cn: 这一族的每个形式都带着表示追求的 pet- 词基。

items.meaning: in a way that competes well
items.exampleCN: 这个团队的报价很有竞争力。
这份报告给各国竞争力排名。
每位参赛者都领到一个徽章。

items.example: Two competitors withdrew at the start.
They compete on service, not price.
items.exampleCN: 他们比的是服务而不是价格。
相互竞争的说法让买家糊涂了。

definition_en: to say that you are unhappy or not satisfied about something
core_image: 饭桌上有人皱着眉头把盘子往前一推
scene: 楼上整夜装修，邻居第二天一早就去了物业。She complained about the noise for a week.
sceneCN: 这里 complain 指「投诉；抱怨」（第 1 个义项：表达不满）；句意是她为这噪音抱怨了一周。

senses.title: To say you are unhappy
senses.definition: to say that something is wrong or annoying
senses.definitionCN: 说出某事不对或令人烦
senses.example: He complained about the cold soup.
senses.exampleCN: 他抱怨汤是凉的。
senses.why: The oldest sense is simply giving voice to a private displeasure.
senses.whyCN: 最古老的义项只是把心里的不快说出来。

senses.title: To make a formal protest
senses.definition: to tell an authority that something is wrong
senses.definitionCN: 向管理方说明某事有问题
senses.example: Guests complained to the manager about the room.
senses.exampleCN: 客人向经理投诉房间问题。
senses.why: When the listener has power to act, a complaint becomes a formal claim.
senses.whyCN: 当听者有权处理，抱怨就成了正式投诉。

senses.title: To describe a pain or illness
senses.definition: to say that you feel pain somewhere
senses.definitionCN: 说自己某处疼痛
senses.example: She complained of a headache all morning.
senses.exampleCN: 她一上午都在说头痛。
senses.why: Pain, once spoken, becomes a symptom a doctor can read.
senses.whyCN: 疼痛一旦说出，就成了医生能读的症状。

intro.en: Complain comes from Latin plangere, to beat the breast in grief, through Old French complaindre.
intro.cn: complain 经古法语 complaindre 上溯到拉丁语 plangere，意为悲伤地捶胸。

items.en: Plangere meant to strike the breast and lament.
items.cn: plangere 意为捶胸哀叹。

items.en: The word shifted from mourning to voicing any grief.
items.cn: 这个词从哀悼转向说出任何悲伤。

items.en: Old French complaindre brought it into daily speech.
items.cn: 古法语 complaindre 把它带进日常语言。

items.en: English complain first meant to lament a loss.
items.cn: 英语 complain 最初指为损失而哀叹。

items.en: It settled into grumbling, formal protest and naming a pain.
items.cn: 后来它稳定为抱怨、正式投诉与说出病痛。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close in shape to complain, and the meaning group ranks grumbling, protesting and formal objection.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 complain 形状相近的词，近义组排出嘟囔、抗议与正式反对。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a plate pushed away, then move to a formal complaint and to pain that is finally spoken.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从被推开的盘子开始，再走到正式投诉以及终于说出口的疼痛。

normal.en: Complain about a thing, complain to a person, complain of a pain.
normal.cn: 对事情用 complain about，对人用 complain to，说疼痛用 complain of。

normal.en: The noun is complaint, and it is one letter away from complain.
normal.cn: 名词是 complaint，与 complain 只差一点。

normal.en: A complainer finds a flaw in every meal.
normal.cn: 爱抱怨的人每顿饭都能挑出毛病。

normal.en: Complaining to a manager turns a grumble into a case.
normal.cn: 向经理抱怨，就把嘟囔变成了一桩案子。

normal.en: The old root means to beat the breast, so the word began in grief.
normal.cn: 古老词根意为捶胸，所以这个词起于悲伤。

abstract.en: Picture a spoon set down a little too hard.
abstract.cn: 想象勺子被放得稍重了一点。

abstract.en: Picture a guest writing a long note at the front desk.
abstract.cn: 想象客人在前台写一张长长的意见。

abstract.en: Picture a patient pointing at the chest and frowning.
abstract.cn: 想象病人指着胸口皱眉。

examples.en: Customers complained about the slow service.
examples.cn: 顾客抱怨服务太慢。

examples.en: Stop complaining and help me carry this.
examples.cn: 别抱怨了，帮我抬一下这个。

examples.en: He complained of chest pain at midnight.
examples.cn: 他半夜说胸口疼。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 complain 记成 com（一起）加 plain（捶胸）：一起捶着胸说委屈，就是抱怨。

root: 源自拉丁语 plangere（捶胸哀叹）与古法语 complaindre，本义是为不幸而捶胸出声，后引申为抱怨、投诉与诉说病痛。

sensesIntro.en: From voicing a small annoyance, to a formal claim, and finally to naming a pain.
sensesIntro.cn: 从说出小小的不快，到正式投诉，最后到说出病痛。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: someone at a table pushing the plate away with a frown.
core.cn: 核心意象：饭桌上有人皱着眉头把盘子往前一推。

branches.en: Saying you are unhappy is the plainest sense.
branches.cn: 说出自己不开心，是最朴素的义项。

branches.en: A complaint to someone in power becomes official.
branches.cn: 向有权处理的人抱怨，就变成正式的。

branches.en: Pain spoken aloud becomes a symptom.
branches.cn: 疼痛说出口，就成了症状。

branches.en: Both senses begin with the same displeasure.
branches.cn: 两个义项都从同一种不快开始。

branches.en: Both hand the trouble to someone who can act.
branches.cn: 两者都把麻烦交给能处理的人。

intro.en: Complain is a verb from Old French complaindre, built on the Latin lament base plangere.
intro.cn: complain 是来自古法语 complaindre 的动词，建立在拉丁语表示哀叹的词基 plangere 上。

latinIntro.en: The same root survives in plangent, a sound that is loud and mournful.
latinIntro.cn: 同一个词根还留在 plangent 里，指响亮而哀伤的声音。

items.meaning: says he or she is unhappy

items.example: They complained to the front desk.
Complaining will not fix the lift.
The manager knew every complainer by name.
items.exampleCN: 经理叫得出每个爱抱怨的客人的名字。
她的投诉很快得到处理。

items.meaning: a person who makes a formal complaint

definition_en: a statement that you are not satisfied, or an illness that troubles you
core_image: 信箱里塞着一张写满字的意见卡

senses.title: A statement of dissatisfaction
senses.definition: a statement that something is wrong or annoying
senses.definitionCN: 说明某事有问题或令人烦的话
senses.example: My main complaint is the noise at night.
senses.exampleCN: 我主要的抱怨是夜里的噪音。
senses.why: The noun holds the words that the verb lets out.
senses.whyCN: 这个名词装着动词说出口的那些话。

senses.title: A formal protest
senses.definition: an official statement that something is wrong
senses.definitionCN: 向管理方正式说明问题的陈述
senses.example: She filed a complaint with the manager.
senses.exampleCN: 她向经理提交了投诉。
senses.why: Written down and handed to someone with power, a grumble becomes a case.
senses.whyCN: 写下来交给有权处理的人，嘟囔就成了一桩案子。

senses.title: An illness
senses.definition: an illness or a pain in part of the body
senses.definitionCN: 身体某处的病或疼痛
senses.example: The doctor asked about her stomach complaint.
senses.exampleCN: 医生问起她的胃病。
senses.why: A long tradition calls the body's troubles a complaint of the flesh.
senses.whyCN: 很久以来的说法把身体的不适称作肉身的抱怨。

intro.en: Complaint comes from Old French complainte, a noun of lament built on Latin plangere, to beat the breast.
intro.cn: complaint 来自古法语 complainte，这个表示哀叹的名词建立在拉丁语 plangere（捶胸）之上。

items.en: Plangere meant to strike the breast in sorrow.
items.cn: plangere 意为悲伤地捶胸。

items.en: Plangere widened to any loud grieving.
items.cn: plangere 扩展到任何出声的悲悼。

items.en: Old French complainte named the lament itself.
items.cn: 古法语 complainte 指哀叹这件事本身。

items.en: English complaint first meant a lament for a loss.
items.cn: 英语 complaint 最初指为损失而哀叹。

items.en: It came to mean a grumble, a formal case and a bodily illness.
items.cn: 后来它指抱怨、正式案件以及身体的不适。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words one step from complaint, and the meaning group separates a grievance, an objection and an illness.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 complaint 只差一步的词，近义组分辨不满申诉、异议与疾病。

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with a full suggestion box, then move to an official case and to a sickness that has a name.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从塞满的意见箱开始，再走到正式的案子以及有了名字的病。

normal.en: Complaint is what is left after someone has complained.
normal.cn: complaint 就是有人抱怨过之后留下来的东西。

normal.en: Make a complaint, file a complaint, lodge a complaint: all three are common.
normal.cn: 提出、提交、正式递交投诉，三种说法都常见。

normal.en: A minor complaint at the doctor is a small illness.
normal.cn: 在医生那里说的小 complaint，就是小毛病。

normal.en: The spelling changes from complain to complaint; keep the t.
normal.cn: 从 complain 变 complaint 时要留住结尾的 t。

normal.en: A complaint is a complaint whether it is spoken, written or felt in the body.
normal.cn: 无论说出口、写下来还是落在身体里，它都是 complaint。

abstract.en: Picture a card box so full that the lid will not shut.
abstract.cn: 想象意见卡多到盒盖合不上。

abstract.en: Picture a form with a room number written in the corner.
abstract.cn: 想象一张表格，角上写着房间号。

abstract.en: Picture a patient listing symptoms one by one.
abstract.cn: 想象病人一条条说出症状。

examples.en: The manager listened to every complaint politely.
examples.cn: 经理礼貌地听完每一条投诉。

examples.en: He made a complaint about the broken seat.
examples.cn: 他就坏掉的座位提出了投诉。

examples.en: Her only complaint was a mild cough.
examples.cn: 她唯一的不适是轻微的咳嗽。

sensesIntro.en: From a voiced grumble, to an official case, and finally to an illness of the body.
sensesIntro.cn: 从说出口的嘟囔，到正式的案子，最后到身体的不适。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a complaint card crammed into a small hotel letterbox.
core.cn: 核心意象：信箱里塞着一张写满字的意见卡。

branches.en: The spoken grumble is the everyday sense.
branches.cn: 说出口的嘟囔是日常义项。

branches.en: Written and filed, the grumble becomes a case.
branches.cn: 写下来归档，嘟囔就成了一桩案子。

branches.en: The body also makes complaints, and doctors name them.
branches.cn: 身体也会抱怨，医生给它们命名。

branches.en: Both are words pointed at something wrong.
branches.cn: 两者都是指向某个问题的言语。

branches.en: Both are recorded, one on paper and one in a file of health.
branches.cn: 两者都会被记录，一个记在纸上，一个记在病历里。

intro.en: Complaint is the noun matching the verb complain, formed with a final -t.
intro.cn: complaint 是与动词 complain 对应的名词，以结尾的 -t 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin lament base plangere also survives in plangent.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示哀叹的词基 plangere 也留在 plangent 里。

items.example: The office handles hundreds of complaints.
items.exampleCN: 这个办公室处理数百条投诉。

items.meaning: says he or she is unhappy
the person who files a complaint
items.example: The complainant gave a short statement.

definition_en: to finish making something whole, or having every part and nothing missing
core_image: 最后一块拼图落位，整幅画终于没有缺口
scene: 木匠把最后一块板钉上，柜子刚好合缝。It took him a month to complete the cabinet.
sceneCN: 这里 complete 指「完成」（第 1 个义项：做完某事）；句意是他花了一个月才把柜子做完。

senses.title: To finish
senses.definition: to finish doing or making something
senses.definitionCN: 做完或制成某物
senses.example: She completed the report before noon.
senses.exampleCN: 她中午前完成了报告。
senses.why: The verb looks at the last step that closes a gap.
senses.whyCN: 动词着眼于补上缺口的那最后一步。

senses.title: Whole, with nothing missing
senses.definition: having every part and no gaps
senses.definitionCN: 各部分齐全、没有缺漏
senses.example: The museum owns a complete set of these coins.
senses.exampleCN: 博物馆藏有这套钱币的完整一套。
senses.why: The adjective describes the state the last step leaves behind.
senses.whyCN: 形容词描述最后一步留下的状态。

senses.title: Total and thorough
senses.definition: used to stress that something is total
senses.definitionCN: 用来强调某事是彻底的
senses.example: The plan was a complete failure.
senses.exampleCN: 这个计划彻底失败了。
senses.why: If nothing is missing, the whole thing can also be called complete in degree.
senses.whyCN: 若一无所缺，整体在程度上也可称作彻底。

intro.en: Complete comes from Latin complere, to fill up, from com, completely, and plere, to fill.
intro.cn: complete 来自拉丁语 complere，意为填满，由 com（完全）与 plere（填充）构成。

items.en: Plere meant to fill something up.
items.cn: plere 意为把某物填满。

items.en: Complere meant to fill until nothing was missing.
items.cn: complere 意为填到一点不缺。

items.en: Completus described a thing fully filled.
items.cn: completus 描述被完全填满的事物。

items.en: Old French complet kept the sense of whole.
items.cn: 古法语 complet 保留了「完整」的意思。

items.en: English complete grew both a verb and an adjective use.
items.cn: 英语 complete 长出动词与形容词两种用法。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words one letter from complete, and the meaning group separates finishing, wholeness and total degree.
note.cn: 形近组收的是与 complete 只差一个字母的词，近义组分辨做完、完整与彻底程度。

entries.definition: to strive against others
a statement of dissatisfaction
to add what is missing
to bring something to an end
whole, with nothing left out
complete in amount

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with the last puzzle piece, then move to the whole it leaves and to the total degree it can name.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从最后一块拼图开始，再走到它留下的整体以及它能表示的彻底程度。

normal.en: Com- means fully and plere means fill, so complete is filled to the top.
normal.cn: com- 表示完全，plere 表示填满，complete 就是填到顶。

normal.en: As a verb, complete means to close the last gap.
normal.cn: 作动词时，complete 意为补上最后的缺口。

normal.en: As an adjective, complete means no part is missing.
normal.cn: 作形容词时，complete 意为没有一部分缺失。

normal.en: A complete failure is not a finished one, but a total one.
normal.cn: a complete failure 不是「完成了的失败」，而是「彻底的失败」。

normal.en: The noun is completion, and the opposite adjective is incomplete.
normal.cn: 名词是 completion，反面形容词是 incomplete。

abstract.en: Picture a puzzle with only one empty space left.
abstract.cn: 想象一幅拼图只剩一个小空格。

abstract.en: Picture a full set of keys on one ring.
abstract.cn: 想象一整串钥匙挂在一个环上。

abstract.en: Picture a room so quiet that the clock is loud.
abstract.cn: 想象房间静得连钟声都显得响。

examples.en: Please complete the form in black ink.
examples.cn: 请用黑色墨水填完这张表。

examples.en: The collection is now complete.
examples.cn: 这套收藏现在完整了。

examples.en: His answer was complete nonsense.
examples.cn: 他的回答完全是胡扯。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 complete 记成 com（一起）加 plete（填满）：把空缺全填满，就是完成与完整。

root: 源自拉丁语 complere，com- 表示全部，plere 表示填满，本义是填满、使无空缺，后引申为完成、完整的与彻底的。

sensesIntro.en: From the last step that fills a gap, to the whole that results, and finally to total degree.
sensesIntro.cn: 从填上缺口的最后一步，到由此得到的整体，最后到彻底的程度。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: the last piece clicks in and the picture has no empty space.
core.cn: 核心意象：最后一块拼图落位，整幅画终于没有缺口。

branches.en: The verb names the act of closing the gap.
branches.cn: 动词指补上缺口的那个动作。

branches.en: The adjective names the whole that no longer has a gap.
branches.cn: 形容词指不再有缺口的整体。

branches.en: If nothing is missing, the degree can also be called complete.
branches.cn: 若一无所缺，程度也可以叫彻底。

branches.en: The act and the state are two sides of one filling.
branches.cn: 动作与状态是同一次填充的两面。

branches.en: A whole thing can also be wholly one way.
branches.cn: 一个完整的东西，也可以在程度上完全是某种样子。

intro.en: Complete is built on Latin com, fully, plus plere, to fill.
intro.cn: complete 由拉丁语 com（完全）加 plere（填充）构成。

latinIntro.en: The filling base plere also appears in supply and in supplement.
latinIntro.cn: 表示填充的词基 plere 也出现在 supply 与 supplement 里。

items.example: She completes each task on time.
items.exampleCN: 她按时完成每一项任务。

items.example: The bridge was completed in May.
Completing the form takes five minutes.
The editor checks the completeness of the file.
items.exampleCN: 编辑检查文件是否完整。

definition_en: in every way, to the greatest degree, or with nothing left out
core_image: 杯子被倒空，倒过来连一滴也不剩
scene: 雨停了，窗外的街道被洗得没有一丝灰尘。The room was completely silent after they left.
sceneCN: 这里 completely 指「完全地；彻底地」（第 1 个义项：达到全部程度）；句意是他们走后房间一片寂静。

senses.title: To the greatest degree
senses.definition: used to say that something is as strong or as full as possible
senses.definitionCN: 用来说某事物达到最强的程度
senses.example: I completely agree with your plan.
senses.exampleCN: 我完全同意你的方案。
senses.why: The adverb pushes an adjective or verb all the way to its limit.
senses.whyCN: 这个副词把形容词或动词推到极限。

senses.title: With nothing left out
senses.definition: in every part, so that nothing is missing
senses.definitionCN: 在每一部分上，没有一点遗漏
senses.example: The old house was completely rebuilt.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老房子被彻底重建了。
senses.why: Here the stress falls on coverage: every part is touched.
senses.whyCN: 这里强调的是覆盖：每一部分都被涉及。

intro.en: Completely is the adverb of complete, from Latin complere, to fill up.
intro.cn: completely 是 complete 的副词形式，后者来自拉丁语 complere，意为填满。

items.en: Plere meant to fill, and complere meant to fill fully.
items.cn: plere 意为填充，complere 意为填满。

items.en: Completus described something with nothing missing.
items.cn: completus 描述毫无缺失的事物。

items.en: Old French complet passed the adjective into English.
items.cn: 古法语 complet 把这个形容词传进英语。

items.en: English added -ly to make the adverb of manner.
items.cn: 英语加上 -ly，构成表示方式的副词。

items.en: Completely became one of the commonest intensifiers.
items.cn: completely 成了最常用的强调词之一。

note.en: The look-alike group holds forms of the same complete family, and the meaning group ranks entirely, totally and fully.
note.cn: 形近组收的是 complete 家族的形式，近义组排出 entirely、totally 与 fully 的强弱。

entries.definition: to finish something
the act of finishing
not finished and not whole
in every way
to the full amount
completely, or at least enough

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with an emptied cup, then move to the strongest degree and to coverage with no gaps.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从倒空的杯子开始，再走到最强程度与毫无缺漏的覆盖。

normal.en: Complete means filled, and -ly turns it into filled to the last drop.
normal.cn: complete 是填满，加 -ly 就是填到最后一滴。

normal.en: Completely different means no part is the same.
normal.cn: completely different 指没有一处相同。

normal.en: Completely free is not partly free.
normal.cn: completely free 不是部分免费。

normal.en: Not completely sure is a polite way to doubt.
normal.cn: not completely sure 是礼貌地表示怀疑。

normal.en: The adverb almost always sits before the word it pushes.
normal.cn: 这个副词几乎总放在它所推动的词前面。

abstract.en: Picture a cup turned over and shaken, not a drop falling.
abstract.cn: 想象杯子倒过来抖一抖，一滴也不落。

abstract.en: Picture a room with every window shut and no sound at all.
abstract.cn: 想象房间每扇窗都关着，没有一点声音。

abstract.en: Picture a wall repainted from corner to corner.
abstract.cn: 想象一面墙从一角到另一角重新刷过。

examples.en: The two sisters are completely different in temper.
examples.cn: 这两姐妹的性情完全不同。

examples.en: He completely forgot the appointment.
examples.cn: 他把约会忘得一干二净。

examples.en: The tunnel was completely dark for a minute.
examples.cn: 隧道里有一分钟漆黑一片。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 completely 记成 complete（完整的）加 ly：做到一点不缺，就是完全地。

root: 由 complete（完整的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，本义是以毫无缺漏的方式，后引申为完全地、彻底地。

sensesIntro.en: From the strongest degree, to full coverage with nothing missing.
sensesIntro.cn: 从最强的程度，到毫无遗漏的覆盖。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: an emptied cup held upside down, not a drop left.
core.cn: 核心意象：杯子被倒空，倒过来连一滴也不剩。

branches.en: The first sense intensifies a feeling or a judgement.
branches.cn: 第一个义项把感受或判断推到最强。

branches.en: The second sense covers every part of a thing.
branches.cn: 第二个义项覆盖一件事的每一部分。

branches.en: Both come from the same image of a cup filled to the top.
branches.cn: 两者都来自同一个杯子被填满的意象。

branches.en: In speech it often softens a strong claim, as in not completely sure.
branches.cn: 在口语里它常让强硬的判断变软，比如 not completely sure。

branches.en: Rebuilding a house completely means touching every wall.
branches.cn: 把房子彻底重建，意味着每一面墙都动过。

intro.en: Completely is the adjective complete plus the adverb ending -ly.
intro.cn: completely 是形容词 complete 加副词后缀 -ly 构成。

latinIntro.en: The Latin filling base plere is still visible under the English word.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语表示填充的词基 plere 仍能在这层英语下面看见。

items.example: The work was completed on time.
Completing the course takes a year.
They checked the completeness of the set.
items.exampleCN: 他们检查了这套东西是否完整。

definition_en: made of many connected parts that are hard to understand, or a group of buildings, or a strong feeling fixed in the mind
core_image: 一团缠在一起的线，越拉越紧
scene: 新小区里有住宅、商铺和一所小学，走进去容易迷路。The new complex includes homes, shops and a school.
sceneCN: 这里 complex 指「综合体」（第 2 个义项：由多部分组成的建筑群）；句意是这个新综合体包含住宅、商铺和一所小学。

senses.title: Hard to understand
senses.definition: having many parts that are connected in ways hard to follow
senses.definitionCN: 由许多部分以难以理清的方式相连
senses.example: The tax rules are far too complex for most people.
senses.exampleCN: 税法对大多数人来说太复杂了。
senses.why: Many parts plus many links is exactly what makes a thing hard to hold in the mind.
senses.whyCN: 部分多、牵连多，正是事物难以在脑中把握的原因。

senses.title: A group of buildings
senses.definition: a group of buildings or facilities used for one purpose
senses.definitionCN: 为同一用途建起的一组建筑或设施
senses.example: The sports complex has two pools and a gym.
senses.exampleCN: 这个体育中心有两个泳池和一间健身房。
senses.why: Parts gathered on one site become a whole that carries one name.
senses.whyCN: 聚集在同一场地上的部分，成了一个共用一个名字的整体。

senses.title: A fixed feeling
senses.definition: a strong feeling or idea that is fixed in a person's mind
senses.definitionCN: 牢牢盘踞在人心里的强烈感受或念头
senses.example: He still has a complex about his accent.
senses.exampleCN: 他对自己的口音仍有心结。
senses.why: Psychology borrowed the word for feelings woven so tightly that they hold the mind.
senses.whyCN: 心理学借这个词，指缠绕得紧紧、抓住人心的感受。

intro.en: Complex comes from Latin complecti, to embrace or intertwine, whose participle is complexus.
intro.cn: complex 来自拉丁语 complecti，意为拥抱或交织，其分词形式是 complexus。

items.en: Plectere meant to weave or to twine.
items.cn: plectere 意为编织或缠绕。

items.en: Complecti meant to wrap around and hold together.
items.cn: complecti 意为缠绕包围、抱在一起。

items.en: Complexus described things woven into one.
items.cn: complexus 描述被织成一体的东西。

items.en: English complex first meant made of connected parts.
items.cn: 英语 complex 最初指由相互连接的部分组成。

items.en: It expanded to building groups and to fixed feelings.
items.cn: 后来它扩展到建筑群以及盘踞不去的感受。

note.en: The look-alike group holds words close to complex in sound, and the meaning group ranks complicated, intricate and a network of parts.
note.cn: 形近组收的是读音与 complex 相近的词，近义组排出复杂难懂、错综复杂与相互连接的部分。

hard to understand because of many parts
having many small parts arranged finely

normalIntro.en: These hooks begin with tangled thread, then move to many buildings on one site and to a knot held in the mind.
normalIntro.cn: 这些记忆钩子从缠住的线开始，再走到同一场地上的一片建筑以及心里的一个结。

normal.en: Com- is together and plex means weave, so complex is woven together.
normal.cn: com- 是一起，plex 是编织，complex 就是被织在一起。

normal.en: Many parts plus many links equals complex.
normal.cn: 部分多、连接多，就等于复杂。

normal.en: A sports complex is one site holding many facilities.
normal.cn: 体育综合体就是一块场地上装着许多设施。

normal.en: An inferiority complex is a knot that keeps pulling tight.
normal.cn: 自卑情结就是一个越拉越紧的结。

normal.en: Complex is the thing; complexity is the quality it has.
normal.cn: complex 是那个东西，complexity 是它具备的性质。

abstract.en: Picture a ball of thread where one pull tightens everything.
abstract.cn: 想象一团线，一拉反而更紧。

abstract.en: Picture one gate opening onto homes, shops and a school.
abstract.cn: 想象一道门后连着住宅、商铺和学校。

abstract.en: Picture a single thought that keeps returning at night.
abstract.cn: 想象一个念头，夜里总是回来。

examples.en: The human brain is a highly complex organ.
examples.cn: 人脑是一个极其复杂的器官。

examples.en: They built a new shopping complex near the station.
examples.cn: 他们在车站附近建了一个新的购物中心。

examples.en: He has a complex about being short.
examples.cn: 他对个子矮有心结。

dict_mnemonic.text: 把 complex 记成 com（一起）加 plex（编织）：许多线一起编在一块，就是复杂的。

root: 源自拉丁语 complecti（缠绕、拥抱）与 complexus，本义是交织在一起的，后引申为复杂的、综合体与情结。

sensesIntro.en: From many tangled parts, to many buildings on one site, and finally to a knot in the mind.
sensesIntro.cn: 从交织的许多部分，到同一场地上的一片建筑，最后到心里的一个结。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a ball of thread tangled so tightly that pulling makes it worse.
core.cn: 核心意象：一团缠在一起的线，越拉越紧。

branches.en: Many parts and many links make the first sense.
branches.cn: 部分多、连接多，造出了第一个义项。

branches.en: Buildings gathered on one site carry the same name.
branches.cn: 聚在同一场地的建筑沿用同一个名字。

branches.en: A feeling woven that tightly becomes a complex.
branches.cn: 一种感受缠得那么紧，就成了情结。

branches.en: Both senses gather parts into one whole.
branches.cn: 两个义项都把部分聚成一个整体。

branches.en: A tangle in the world and a tangle in the mind share one image.
branches.cn: 世上的乱麻与心里的乱麻共用一个意象。

intro.en: Complex is built on Latin com, together, plus plectere, to weave.
intro.cn: complex 由拉丁语 com（一起）加 plectere（编织）构成。

latinIntro.en: The weaving base also appears in perplex, to weave someone into confusion.
latinIntro.cn: 表示编织的词基也出现在 perplex 里，意为把人织进困惑。

items.meaning: more than one complex or complex feeling
items.example: The city has three sports complexes.
items.exampleCN: 这座城市有三个体育中心。

items.example: The complexity of the rules surprised us.
items.exampleCN: 规则的复杂程度让我们吃惊。

items.example: She explained the complexities of the case.
items.exampleCN: 她解释了案子的复杂之处。

items.meaning: the natural colour of the skin
items.example: The sea air improved his complexion.
items.exampleCN: 海边的空气改善了他的肤色。

items.example: People of all complexions work here.
items.exampleCN: 各种肤色的人都在这里工作。

items.meaning: a problem that makes things harder
